title: A simulated turn without rightward growth
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality, let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, choose $a_0\in\Gamma$, and let $x$ be a word over the enlarged sweep alphabet of $M$. Let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on the input obtained by retracting each symbol of $x$ using $a_0$, let $q$ be a state of $M$, and let $s$ assign to each work tape an optional symbol and a Boolean flag. Suppose the symbols recorded by $s$ are exactly those scanned in $c$, and no tape flagged by $s$ has a transition that moves its head to the right. For any integer $z$ and finite left stack $l$, the simulator takes one step from the forward-sweep configuration at the input position of $c$, with frontier $z$, left stack $l$, right stack consisting of the boundary marker, and output equal to the embedded output of $c$, to the backward-sweep configuration at the input position after $M$'s prescribed transition, with frontier $z-1$, left stack consisting of the boundary marker, right stack $l$, and output equal to the embedded output after that transition. At both the initial and final configurations, the simulator's work-head position lies between $z-1$ and $z$, inclusive.
